newsitem.title: USA: NYS comptroller faults labor agency for oversight.
newsitem.headline: NYS comptroller faults labor agency for oversight.

text.p: The New York State comptroller on Tuesday faulted the state Department of Labor for not collecting fines from public agencies swiftly enough to ensure that employees are protected.
"I urge the Department of Labor to use this audit as an opportunity to improve their oversight of public employees' safety and health," said H. Carl McCall in prepared remarks.
He explained that if agencies did not risk financial penalties, they might not move quickly enough to correct unsafe situations.
At the same time, the state comptroller found that the number of inspections of workplace problems fell by 18 percent between the federal fiscal years of 1994 and 1995.

While the state Department of Corrections owes more than $172,000 in penalities for unsafe conditions, there is no system in place to make sure that any funds owed by state agencies can be collected, McCall said.
